chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ṣāliḥ ibn al-Sindī, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) about the testimony of the child of zina: “Is it valid?” He said: “No.”
So I said: “Al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtaybah claims that it is valid.” He said: “O Allah, do not forgive his sin.”
Allah did not say to al-Ḥakam: “Indeed, it is surely a reminder for you and your people.”
So let al-Ḥakam go right and left; for by Allah, knowledge is not taken except from a Household upon whom Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) descended.

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ: the People of the Household, i.e. Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; a form of supplication
key_terms.شَهَادَةِ: legal testimony given in a judicial context

ai.seo_question: From whom should religious knowledge be taken, and what is the ruling on the testimony of a child of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that the testimony of one born from zina is not accepted. It also emphasizes that true religious knowledge is to be taken from Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام), and not from those outside their authority, while invoking a Qur'anic phrase to deny al-Ḥakam any special claim to it.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sindy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Aban Bin usman, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the testimony of a son of adultery (bastard), ‘Is it allowed?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
So I said, ‘Al-Hakam Bin Oteyba is alleging that it is allowed?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Do not Forgive his sins.
Allahazwj did not Say to Al Hakam [43:44] And it is a Reminder for you and your people.

So let Al-Hakam go right and left, for, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, he will not find the knowledge except from the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Household. Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> descends unto them<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindi from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from abu Basir who has said the following.
“I askked abu Ja‘far (a.s.) about the permissibility of the testimony of a person born out of wedlock.” He said, “No, it is not addissible.”
I then said, “Al-Hakam ibn ‘Utayba believes it is addmissible.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “O Lord, do not forgive his sin.
Allah has not to al-Hakam, “ It (the Quran) is a reminder to you and to your people . .” [43:44]
Al-Hakam may go right or left, by Allah, the knowledge worthwhile to learn comes only from Ahl al-Bayt (members of the family of Prophet Muhammad) to who Jibril came down.”
